title: Search Box Spell Check
statement: A shop's search box suggests the closest product name when a customer makes a typo. For a typed word and each of 5,000 product names (up to 30 letters each), it needs the fewest insertions, deletions and replacements.

approaches.name: Edit-distance DP on a table of prefixes for each name
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: About 4.5 million cells in total; exact and fast.

approaches.name: Recursion on (i, j) with memoization
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Same bound; more memory and call overhead.

approaches.name: Count letters the two words share
approaches.label: unsuitable

approaches.name: Generate every edit sequence until the words match
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Far too many sequences even for short words.

title: Delivery Van Loader
statement: A courier van carries at most 2,000 kg. Today there are 150 parcels, each with a weight and a delivery fee; each parcel goes in whole or waits for tomorrow. The dispatcher wants the largest total fee.

approaches.name: 0/1 knapsack DP over capacities, capacities from high to low
approaches.label: best

approaches.name: Take parcels by highest fee per kilogram until full
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Wrong for whole parcels: a high-ratio parcel can waste space that two others would fill.

approaches.name: Full 2-D table over parcels and capacities
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Same time, more memory; useful to list which parcels were taken.

title: Gene Sequence Similarity
statement: A biology lab compares two gene sequences of up to 5,000 letters (A, C, G, T) and wants the length of the longest sequence of letters that appears in both in the same order, with gaps allowed.

approaches.name: Longest-common-subsequence DP with one or two rows
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: 25 million cells, fast in a compiled language; two rows keep memory small.

approaches.name: LCS with the full n × m table
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Needed to print the shared sequence, but 25 million cells of memory.

approaches.name: Longest common substring with a sliding comparison
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Answers a different question: gaps are not allowed.
